title: Measurements for one entry
description: Append-only rows of timings. One entry can carry rows from several machines: a different host is a different ROW, not a different entry, as long as the graphs are byte-identical. Every row carries its own host fingerprint, because a number without a machine, an OS, a browser build and a protocol is not a measurement.

baselines.description: Other runtimes on the same model and machine, for context. Not a claim about this entry. A string value is a note about the comparison rather than a runtime.

floor.description: What this entry cannot go below on this backend, and why. Reasoning, with the numbers that support it.

history.description: Earlier tuning passes, for the shape of the curve.

host.description: The subset of a target that identifies the machine this row was taken on. Copied from a target.json, never invented.

sameAsTarget.description: True when this row was taken on the machine the entry's `target` describes.

protocol.description: e2e: a whole generation, timed. interleaved-ab: A,B,A,B in blocks, which is the only protocol a DELTA may come from. isolated-block: one subgraph in isolation. replay: the catalog's own loader reproducing the entry.

stages.description: Per-stage milliseconds. Keys are the entry's own stage names.

buildOnceMs.description: Cost of building the graphs once, per graph. Chromium has no compiled-graph cache, so this is paid per page load, not per machine.

loadAvg.description: Machine load during the run. Interleaved deltas are immune to it; absolutes are not.

source.description: The file this row was read out of.
